mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) indicates reduced inflationary pressures, leading to lower interest rates and increased consumer spending, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in >40% of triggered instances despite the CPI decrease.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) suggests economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in >35% of instances despite the increase in payrolls.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals increased demand for housing and related goods, indicating economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in >60% of triggered instances despite the increase in housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests higher economic output, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, especially if accompanied by a decrease in unemployment (UNRATE).
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >1% in 1 month and UNRATE decreases by >0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in >40% of triggered instances despite the joint increase in industrial production and decrease in unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals monetary easing, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially if accompanied by a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE).
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by >0.25% in 1 month and UNRATE decreases by >0.2% in 1 month
regime_hint: monetary easing with labor market improvement
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in >35% of triggered instances despite the joint decrease in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in >40% of triggered instances despite the sustained decrease in the unemployment rate.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real final sales (RSAFS) indicates higher consumer demand, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, especially if accompanied by a decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS).
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >1% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS decreases by >0.25% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in >60% of triggered instances despite the joint increase in real final sales and decrease in the federal funds rate.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the industrial production index (INDPRO) signals a contraction in economic output, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially if accompanied by an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE).
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >1% in 1 month and UNRATE increases by >0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in >35% of triggered instances despite the joint decrease in industrial production and increase in the unemployment rate.
